# Revisit pandoc spawn cost on the DC render path (after `rich_sha` lands)

Deferred from `ashy-waterlog-hamadryas` (5c0e), where safe-run batching was DESCOPED by operator decision. Park this until the cutover story's change-gated `rich_sha` skip has landed and real spawn cost can be measured against it; the skip avoids rendering unchanged bodies entirely and may remove the problem outright.

## The hazard
The DC renderer spawns one pandoc process per renderable unit: ~0.3s/field flat spawn cost independent of body size, and a serial reconcile over many fields was measured blocking ~20 min of wall time on `fork+exec`.

## What was already measured (starting point — do not redo)
Against the landed renderer (merged `cf5155e528`) over the committed 178-body corpus in `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`:
- 233 contiguous SAFE runs across 884 `_RENDER` units. Ceiling = 74% fewer spawns, but **106 of 233 runs (46%) are a single unit**, so it is unreachable.
- Run-level fallback (one bad fragment poisons the run): **63/178 bodies (35%) lose richness**.
- Verify-then-accept with per-unit fallback: 157/178 identical to per-unit, but only **12% fewer spawns**, because a failed batch pays for both attempts.
- **21/178 bodies render DIFFERENTLY even when a batch verifies.** pandoc parses block boundaries relative to surrounding content, so concatenating units into one commonmark document is not equivalent to rendering them separately. Suspected causes: setext-style headings, lazy continuation, reference-style links.

## Where to start if this is picked up
The 21 divergent bodies are the whole question. Characterise them first: if a document-assembly rule (for example forcing an unambiguous hard block separator between concatenated units, or normalising trailing blank lines) restores byte-equivalence, batching becomes a transparent optimization and the 74%-ceiling argument can be revisited. If it cannot, batching should stay descoped.

Any renewed attempt must keep the invariant this fleet already enforced once: rendered output must not change silently. Prove byte-equality against the per-unit path over the whole corpus before proposing it.
